nodes.label: ShouldDispatchAfterCommit events
nodes.rationale: Dispatching inside a transaction can expose uncommitted data or dispatch work that later rolls back; after-commit dispatch waits for commit and is discarded on rollback.

nodes.label: Retry only safe HTTP operations
nodes.rationale: Retrying state-changing requests without an idempotency guarantee can duplicate side effects.

nodes.label: Bound Work Inside Scheduled Tasks
nodes.rationale: The scheduler cannot terminate arbitrary tasks at a deadline, so commands or jobs must process finite chunks, check deadlines, or dispatch queued work with suitable timeouts.

nodes.label: onOneServer() Shared Lock Identity
nodes.rationale: Scheduler nodes must share an atomic cache store, and named closures need distinct lock identities so each task runs once.

nodes.label: runInBackground() for Independent Tasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks due at the same time otherwise run sequentially; background execution keeps a long independent command from delaying later tasks, but it is limited to command and exec tasks and needs logging.

nodes.label: withoutOverlapping() Lock Expiration
nodes.rationale: The optional value is a lock lease in minutes, not the task timeout; an expiration shorter than the actual run permits overlap, while a lock left too long blocks later runs.

nodes.label: Context-Aware Output Escaping
nodes.rationale: Blade double braces HTML-escape output; raw output is safe only when content is sanitized for the exact HTML context. Escaping rules differ for HTML, URLs, JavaScript, and CSS.

nodes.label: Sensitive Endpoint Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Limiter keys must balance shared-IP grouping against targeted denial of service, and rate limiting never replaces authentication, authorization, or upstream DoS protection.

nodes.label: Mass-Assignment Control with $fillable
nodes.rationale: Models guard all attributes by default; $guarded = [] opts out of that protection, and mass-assignment protection neither validates values nor authorizes the operation.

nodes.label: Policy, Gate, and Form Request Authorization
nodes.norm_label: policy, gate, and form request authorization
nodes.rationale: Authentication alone does not establish permission, and validation is not authorization; protected actions need policies, gates, or form request authorization.

nodes.label: SQL Parameter Binding and Identifier Allow-Lists
nodes.norm_label: sql parameter binding and identifier allow-lists
nodes.rationale: Bindings protect values but not identifiers such as column names or sort directions, so user-selected identifiers must map to an allow-list.

nodes.label: Secrets Out of Application Code
nodes.rationale: Read environment variables in configuration files and use config() in application code so credentials never enter source control and configuration caching still works.

nodes.label: Secure Upload Validation and Storage
nodes.rationale: The mimes rule inspects file content while extensions checks the filename; use storage-generated names and store untrusted files outside publicly executable locations.

nodes.label: Cache::flexible() stale-while-revalidate
nodes.rationale: Serving stale data during a stale window trades freshness for lower latency, and the deferred refresh is not a durable background job.

nodes.label: Chunking large data sets
nodes.rationale: Loading an entire large result set can exceed the practical memory budget, so bounded chunks keep memory use predictable.

nodes.label: Global scopes applied sparingly
nodes.rationale: A global scope silently modifies every query, making queries hard to debug, so it is reserved for universal constraints such as soft deletes or multi-tenancy.

links.description: A 48x46 alpha mask clips a set of feGaussianBlur-filtered ellipses into the mark's silhouette, producing the glowing glassy interior.
An alpha mask and sixteen feGaussianBlur-filtered ellipses in pale lavender (#eee6ff), violet (#8900ff) and cyan (#00c2ff) create the glossy, motion-blurred glow behind the bolt.
The SVG's accessible title is 'Vite' (via aria-labelledby="vite-logo-title") and the artwork is the official Vite brand mark, explicitly identifying the Vite build tool.
The centerpiece is a single angular zigzag lightning-bolt path filled with Vite purple (#9135ff), giving the mark its signature forward-leaning bolt silhouette.
The mark is filled with #863bff violet, shaded with #7e14ff, highlighted with #ede6ff pale lavender and accented with #47bfff cyan ellipses.
The outer path forms a sharp angular emblem built from stacked zigzag ribbon segments with flat shelves and steep diagonals, reading as an abstract lightning-bolt or 'N' monogram.
Two mirrored curved bracket paths use the .parenthesis class, filled black in light mode and switched to white through a prefers-color-scheme: dark media query.

links.evidence: Flat isometric perspective, thin gray outlines, generous white space and soft corner radii match a minimal modern SaaS illustration style.
The image shows two rounded-square plates stacked one above the other in an isometric view, the upper plate floating over the lower one and connected by faint dashed vertical guide lines.
The lower plate has a saturated violet/magenta gradient with a glossy sheen on its extruded side faces; the rest of the image is white with light gray linework.
